title: Distributions, Skewness & Outliers
interviewAnswer: Outliers are not automatically bad data. I first determine whether they are errors, rare but valid cases, or a separate population, then choose transformations, robust statistics or explicit modeling accordingly.

why: Distributions, Skewness & Outliers appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Compare mean vs median under skew.
deepDive: Outliers are not automatically bad data. I first determine whether they are errors, rare but valid cases, or a separate population, then choose transformations, robust statistics or explicit modeling accordingly. Use quantiles/IQR and domain constraints. Log transforms can stabilize heavy right tails. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: A few enterprise customers may be legitimate extreme spenders; deleting them could destroy the business signal.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.

production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
